findings.summary: Stage model is internally inconsistent: requirements define a minimal stage sequence without WorkPlanning/PatchApply/Patch/Plan, while architecture components and tool policy assume additional stages (Plan, WorkPlanning, PatchApply, Patch). This creates ambiguity in checkpoint boundaries, required handoffs, and validator gating.

evidence.note: R4 stage list excludes Plan/WorkPlanning/PatchApply/Patch.
evidence.quote: The Implementation Council workflow SHALL be defined as a deterministic staged state machine with at minimum the stages: Intake → Generate → Validate → Review → Judge → Freeze

evidence.note: Architecture C1 includes Plan and Patch stages (and a different ordering).
evidence.quote: Enforce strict stage ordering and closure gates (Intake → Plan → Generate → Validate → Review → Patch → Judge → Freeze).

evidence.note: Tool policy defines additional stages (WorkPlanning, PatchApply, IntegrateAndValidate) not present in R4.

findings.summary: Executive summary stage flow conflicts with the stated required/selected stage sequence: it claims a single linear flow with Generate → Validate → Judge → Freeze, omitting Review (and other stages referenced elsewhere).

evidence.note: Executive summary omits Review and other stages.
evidence.quote: ...single conservative, linear flow... (Generate → Validate → Judge → Freeze) ...

evidence.note: R4 requires Review stage (at minimum).
evidence.quote: ...Intake → Generate → Validate → Review → Judge → Freeze...

evidence.note: Chosen design decision reiterates the sequence including Review.
evidence.quote: Use a linear, sequential stage order (Intake → Generate → Validate → Review → Judge → Freeze) ...

findings.summary: Tool policy for the Review stage denies artifact_write/workspace_write, but the architecture and requirements require reviewers to emit review_findings.json (a findings artifact). This blocks the reviewer role from producing its mandated output.

evidence.note: Review restrictions deny artifact and workspace writes.
evidence.quote: Reviewers are findings-only; they do not emit canonical writing/patch artifacts.

evidence.note: Explicit deny prevents writing review_findings.json at all (even findings-only).
evidence.quote: deny

evidence.note: Reviewer Pod is required to produce review_findings.json.
evidence.quote: Produce review_findings.json with RFC 6901 evidence pointers into versioned artifacts (CNS6).

findings.summary: Intake stage tool policy allows only non-canonical artifact writes, but the Intake Gate component requires initializing canonical audit-spine artifacts (run_manifest, event_log) and emitting stage_handoff. This is inconsistent with the stated Intake write restrictions.

evidence.note: Intake artifact writes restricted to non-canonical only.
evidence.quote: allow_noncanonical_only

evidence.note: Intake Gate must initialize run_manifest/event_log (canonical).
evidence.quote: Initialize run_manifest and append-only event_log (CNS3).

evidence.note: Intake Gate also must emit a stage_handoff at Intake→Plan boundary.
evidence.quote: Emit stage_handoff for Intake→Plan boundary.

findings.summary: The plan declares a single evidence-pointer object shape ({artifact_ref, entity_id|null, json_pointer, note}) but uses a different structure in decision_log evidence_pointers (includes candidate_id/artifact_id/quote and does not use entity_id). This violates the plan’s own evidence standard requirements.

evidence.note: Glossary defines the evidence pointer object shape with entity_id.
evidence.quote: An RFC 6901 JSON Pointer object {artifact_ref, entity_id|null, json_pointer, note} referencing a versioned JSON artifact location; used as the sole standard...

evidence.note: R10 enforces this single structure.
evidence.quote: ...RFC 6901 JSON Pointer objects with the structure {artifact_ref, entity_id|null, json_pointer, note}...

evidence.note: Decision log uses artifact_id + candidate_id + quote, not entity_id.

findings.summary: R9’s prohibition on “prose/markdown/unstructured text” in canonical artifacts conflicts with the plan’s extensive reliance on freeform natural-language strings in requirements, rationales, risk descriptions, and notes. As written, R9 would imply rejecting artifacts like the plan itself.

evidence.note: R9 prohibits prose/unstructured text in canonical artifacts.
evidence.quote: ...orchestrator SHALL reject any artifact containing prose/markdown/unstructured text...

evidence.note: Example of natural-language requirement text the system would seemingly reject under R9.
evidence.quote: The Implementation Council subsystem SHALL accept exactly one frozen plan_package_final.json...

evidence.note: Example of prose risk description.
evidence.quote: Silent plan-semantics drift / scope expansion: implementation artifacts or code changes effectively alter the meaning...

findings.summary: Tool policy includes an IntegrateAndValidate stage that is not part of the selected O1 sequential pipeline description, suggesting leftover or cross-option stage definitions that may confuse orchestrator stage enforcement and handoff requirements.

evidence.note: Chosen architecture option is O1 (sequential pipeline).
evidence.quote: O1

evidence.note: Tool policy defines IntegrateAndValidate stage.
evidence.quote: IntegrateAndValidate

evidence.note: O1 component list does not define an IntegrateAndValidate stage name (it defines Validate and PatchApply separately only in tool policy).

findings.summary: Requirement R24 (SHOULD decompose large refactors) lacks corresponding acceptance test coverage, weakening enforceability of bounded-change constraints critical to K16 mitigation.

evidence.note: R24 requires decomposition of large refactors but is marked SHOULD, not MUST.
evidence.quote: Large code refactors SHOULD be decomposed into bounded patchsets

evidence.note: No acceptance test explicitly validates R24 patchset size limits or decomposition enforcement.
K16 mitigation depends on patchset size limits that R24 addresses but does not mandate.
evidence.quote: Define patchset size limits... require decomposition

findings.summary: Requirement R25 (SHOULD map test results to AT#) is marked SHOULD but is critical for trace completeness gate (R21) and K13 mitigation; inconsistency between priority and dependency.

evidence.note: R25 is SHOULD priority but trace completeness is a MUST gate.
evidence.quote: test_results.json SHOULD include a deterministic mapping

evidence.note: R21 MUST gate requires trace completeness, which depends on R25.
evidence.quote: trace completeness validators

evidence.note: K13 mitigation requires AT# linkage that R25 addresses as SHOULD.
evidence.quote: validator requires that each AT# has either a passing mapped test

findings.summary: Decision DEC6 mandates deny-by-default network policy, but tool_policy stage definitions for Generate and Validate do not explicitly address package-manager tool allowlisting, creating ambiguity for Q11 resolution.

evidence.note: DEC6 adopts network deny baseline.
evidence.quote: deny-by-default tool permissions (including network deny)

evidence.note: Q11 asks how to handle package-manager operations under network policy.
evidence.quote: dependencies requiring network access and package-manager operations

findings.summary: Architecture O1 chosen option states 'no direct repo writes' in Generate stage, but PatchApply stage allows 'repo_write: allow_via_patch_apply_only', yet no explicit validator or interface contract enforces that Generate cannot invoke patch_apply tool.

evidence.note: Writer Pod (Generate) responsibilities say 'no direct edits' but do not forbid patch_apply tool.
evidence.quote: Produce diff-only patchset JSON artifacts
